newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian forces kill 7 rebels after carnage - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian forces kill 7 rebels after carnage - paper.

text.p: Algerian security forces have killed seven Moslem rebels south of Algeria in the wake of massacres there of villagers, an Algerian newspaper said on Wednesday.
The government forces shot the seven on Tuesday in Houach Germain hamlet in Blida province, some 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, La Tribune daily said.
The rebels were suspected of taking part in the massacres of more than 40 people in the area seven days ago, it said.
At least 250 people have died in the past 10 days in a string of massacres which Algerian newspapers said were carried out by Moslem guerrillas, mainly in villages south of Algiers.

The latest killings brought to about 1,000 the number of people reported slaughtered in a series of mass killings since June 5, when Algeria held a general election which voters and officials hoped would help usher in peace and stability.

Most of the dead, around 700, were civilians, including babies, children and women, some of whom were pregnant. But Algerian newspapers also said that 300 rebels were killed in a two-week government military offensive in July.
The Tribune newspaper said on Wednesday that some women had been also among the rebels suspected of carrying out the recent massacres.

About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
